key_insight: AI-enabled echocardiography can detect prominent epicardial adipose tissue and uncover cardiometabolic risk that is not explained by BMI alone.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help clinicians flag patients with hidden epicardial fat burden using routine ultrasound, supporting earlier risk stratification without requiring advanced imaging.
method: Trained the PanAdipo deep learning model on 1,114,441 echocardiography videos from 28,797 studies labeled by expert report review.
Validated the model across multiple external cohorts, including TTE, POCUS, MIMIC-IV, MESA, and paired cardiac CT datasets.
Compared AI scores with CT-defined epicardial adipose tissue and with cardiometabolic biomarkers and newly documented metabolic disease.
evidence_signal: PanAdipo achieved AUROC 0.86 for report-labeled prominent EAT and up to 0.95 for CT-defined high EAT, while correlating more strongly with indexed EAT volume (rho=0.76) than BMI (rho=0.41).
watch_item: Performance was strongest in retrospective, multi-cohort validation, so prospective testing and workflow integration are still needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile
